findings.title: Second `downsize` definition overrides the 5-arg version
findings.body: Ruby has no overloading, so the new `downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` replaces the earlier `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})`. Existing callers that pass width and height separately now fail or misbehave. A call with 5 positional args raises ArgumentError. A call with 4 args treats max_height as `dimensions` and breaks the dimension string. The earlier definition is dead code and should be removed or renamed.

findings.title: Downsizing loop may leave the file oversized and is not checked for failure
findings.body: `downsize` returns false on failure, but the loop ignores it. It then retries up to 5 times on a failing or no-op conversion, which wastes time. Non-image-convertible or corrupt files proceed unchanged. After the loop, `tempfile.size` may be stale or cached, and the file can still exceed the limit. Upload.create_for then has to reject it, while the client-side check no longer matches the server setting. The 80% conversion also rewrites the file in place, so formats such as GIFs or PNGs may shrink very little.

findings.title: Hard-coded 10MB limit replaces the site-setting limits
findings.body: The client now uses a fixed 10MB limit for all types. This ignores `max_attachment_size_kb`, so attachments above the configured limit pass client validation and are rejected only by the server. Server-side limits are also not tied to this constant. The 413 handler is hard-coded the same way, so the error message may show a wrong limit.

findings.title: API download limit hard-coded to 10MB
findings.body: The API URL download limit no longer follows the site settings. Attachments get a 10MB limit regardless of configuration, and `max_attachment_size_kb` is ignored.
